reason: The table row supports a default of 5 and Adjustable Yes, but the quote and its context give no unit: the qualifier 'measured in vCPUs' and the conditions about automatic increases and lower starting values are not in the evidence; add the page sentence that quotas are managed in vCPUs.
The quote states OS shutdown commands always terminate an instance with an instance store root volume and that you can control stop or terminate for an EBS root volume.

The quotes support one-second increments, a 60-second minimum and all purchase options, with the OS list in context; the condition 'SUSE is billed by the full hour' is not in the quotes or their context.
The quote states per-second billing removes the cost of unused compute time and particularly helps workloads that run over irregular time periods.
The quote states the instance must be in the stopped state before you can change its placement group.
The quote states a single Availability Zone, not isolated to a single rack, and spanning peered VPCs in the same Region.
Under the Cluster placement groups heading the quote states to stop and start all instances and retry, as starting them might migrate them to hardware with capacity.

The quote supports the 5 Gbps limit for internet and Direct Connect traffic of cluster placement groups, but it does not say per what; the scope qualifier 'per cluster placement group' adds an aggregate per-group reading the quote does not state.
The quotes give both recommendations (single launch request, same instance type) and state that adding later or mixing types increases the chance of an insufficient capacity error.
The quote states the recommendation for low latency, high throughput or both, and when most traffic is between instances in the group.

The quote supports that a cluster placement group can't span multiple Availability Zones, but the condition 'it can span peered VPCs in the same Region' is not in this quote or its context; add that quote or drop the condition.
The quote states up to 10 Gbps single-flow inside and up to 5 Gbps outside a cluster placement group, under the enhanced networking rule in context.
The quote states there is no charge for creating a placement group.
The quote states a maximum of 500 placement groups per Region; the condition honestly notes the page names no increase process.
The quotes state Dedicated Hosts can't be launched in placement groups and neither can a Spot Instance configured to stop or hibernate on interruption.
The quotes state one placement group at a time per instance and that placement groups can't be merged.
The quote states placement groups are optional and EC2 tries to spread instances across hardware to minimize correlated failures.
The quote states a partition placement group with Dedicated Instances can have a maximum of two partitions.
The quote states partition groups deploy large distributed and replicated workloads such as HDFS, HBase and Cassandra across distinct racks.
The quote states a maximum of seven partitions per Availability Zone and instance count limited only by account limits; multi-AZ condition is in context.

The quotes support multi-AZ partitions and visibility into which instances are in which partitions, but the claim part 'so that topology-aware applications can use the information' is only in the context sentence after the quote, not in any quote.
The quote states each partition has its own set of racks, each rack has its own network and power source, and no two partitions share racks, isolating hardware failure impact.
The quotes state direct access to high-precision time sources, the microsecond-accurate recommendation, no additional charge, and that the request fails with insufficient hardware.
The quotes state distinct hardware per instance, the recommendation for a small number of critical instances, and reduced risk of simultaneous failures.
The quotes state rack-level groups span multiple AZs with at most seven running instances per AZ and the 21-instance example for three AZs; the Outposts condition is in context.
The quote recommends multiple spread placement groups beyond seven per AZ and says spread is ensured within each group, not across groups.
The quote states spread placement groups are not supported for Dedicated Instances.
The quote states to use private subnets for instances that should not be accessed directly from the internet.
The row under the header 'Default quota per Region' gives 5 public AMIs including those in the Recycle Bin.

The quotes give each rule of thumb: Savings Plans, Reserved Instances or Capacity Reservations per AZ, Capacity Blocks for GPU clusters, Spot for flexible interruptible work, Dedicated for compliance and server-bound licenses.
The seven list quotes match each option and its description, including per-second On-Demand, 1 or 3 year terms, and per-hour Dedicated Instances.
The quote states purchasing options determine how the bill is calculated and Capacity Reservations determine whether capacity is held regardless of use.
The quote states a reboot equals an OS reboot and the instance keeps its host, public DNS name, private IP and instance store data.
The quotes state the recovered instance keeps its instance ID, private and Elastic IP addresses and metadata, and retains a public IP address if it has one.
The quote states RAM data is lost, OS uptime starts over, and with CloudWatch action based recovery instance store data is also lost.
The quote states mechanisms must be configured before a system status check fails, simplified recovery is on by default at launch, and CloudWatch recovery is optional after launch.
The table row under the comparison header gives Metal instance size: Excluded for simplified and Included for CloudWatch action based recovery.
The table row states simplified recovery is not supported with instance store at launch and CloudWatch recovery is supported on selected types with instance store data lost.
The quote states recovery works for a failed system status check (host problem) and does not operate if only the instance status check fails.
The quote states you see only resources tied to the specified Region because Regions are isolated and resources are not automatically replicated.
